overview: Both are cytokines (signalling proteins) of the immune system, but they specialise in different jobs — antiviral defence versus communication between immune cells.
genZNote: Interferon: shouts 'virus alert!' to neighbouring cells. Interleukin: the immune system's internal group chat between cells.

aspects.label: Main Function
aspects.valueA: Interferes with viral replication and alerts neighbouring cells to an antiviral state.
aspects.valueB: Coordinates communication between white blood cells, regulating growth, differentiation, and activation.

aspects.label: Main Trigger for Release
aspects.valueA: Primarily released in response to viral infection.
aspects.valueB: Released by various immune cells during infection, inflammation, or immune activation generally.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Interferon-alpha, used therapeutically for some viral infections and cancers.
aspects.valueB: Interleukin-2 (IL-2), which stimulates T cell proliferation.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Interferons are named for their ability to 'interfere' with viral replication in nearby uninfected cells.
overlay.memoryTrick: Interferon = interferes with viruses. Interleukin = inter-leukocyte (white blood cell) communication.
overlay.commonMisconception: Interferons are not exclusively antiviral in effect — they also have roles in modulating the overall immune response and even some anti-tumour activity.
